q: In a circular motion, how does the object move?
a: It just moves in a circle.
It moves in a straight line.
e: The textbook states that in a circular motion, the object just moves in a circle.

q: Which of the following is given as an example of circular motion?
a: Rotation of earth about its own axis
Motion of the blades of a fan
Artificial satellites going around the earth
e: Artificial satellites going around the earth at a constant height is an example of circular motion.

q: In rotational motion, what does the object do?
a: It just moves in a circle.
It moves with a constant linear velocity.
e: In rotational motion, the object turns about an axis.

q: Which of the following is an example of rotational motion?
a: Artificial satellites going around the earth
Rotation of earth about its own axis
An object moving in a straight line
e: The rotation of earth about its own axis creates the cycle of day and night and is an example of rotational motion.

q: What is a rigid body defined as?
a: A body that does not deform or change shape.
A body that always rotates at a constant angular velocity.
A body that only undergoes linear motion.
e: A rigid body is a body that does not deform or change shape.

q: In a rigid body, what remains constant no matter how the body moves?
a: The angular velocity of the body.
The distance between any two particles within the body.
The tangential acceleration of the particles.
e: No matter how the body moves, the distance between any two particles within the body remains constant.

q: If a rigid body is in rotational motion, what kind of motion do all its particles undergo?
a: Linear motion about a common axis.
Circular motion about a common axis.
Parabolic motion about a common axis.
e: All the particles constituting it undergo circular motion about a common axis.

q: Under what condition is the motion called rotational motion under constant angular acceleration?
a: When the angular velocity is zero.
When the angular velocity changes at a constant rate.
When the linear speed remains constant.
e: If its angular velocity changes at a constant rate, the angular acceleration is constant.

q: Which equation represents the angular speed $\omega$ at time $t$ under constant angular acceleration?
e: The kinematic equation for angular speed is $\omega = \omega_0 + \alpha t$.

q: What does the symbol $\omega_0$ represent in rotational kinematic equations?
e: $\omega_0$ represents the initial angular speed (magnitude of angular velocity at $t=0$).

q: Which equation represents the angular displacement $\theta$ for a time interval $t$?
e: The equation for angular displacement is $\theta = \omega_0 t + \frac{1}{2}\alpha t^2$.

q: Which equation relates $\omega$, $\omega_0$, $\alpha$, and $\theta$?
e: The equation relating these variables without time is $\omega^2 = \omega_0^2 + 2\alpha \theta$.

q: Which equation represents $\theta$ using average angular speed?
e: Angular displacement can be expressed as $\theta = \frac{\omega + \omega_0}{2} t$.

q: The equations for constant angular acceleration are analogous to equations for constant acceleration in which type of motion?
e: The equations are analogous to those for constant acceleration in linear motion.

q: In the analogy between linear and angular motion, what is the angular equivalent of linear velocity $v$?
e: Angular velocity $\omega$ corresponds to linear velocity $v$.

q: In the analogy between linear and angular motion, what is the angular equivalent of linear acceleration $a$?
e: Angular acceleration $\alpha$ corresponds to linear acceleration $a$.

q: In the analogy between linear and angular motion, what is the angular equivalent of linear displacement $s$?
e: Angular displacement $\theta$ corresponds to linear displacement $s$.

q: What is the formula for average angular speed?
e: Average angular speed is given by $\frac{\omega + \omega_0}{2}$.

q: Which linear kinematic equation is analogous to $\omega = \omega_0 + \alpha t$?
e: The linear analogue is $v = v_0 + at$.

q: Which linear kinematic equation is analogous to $\theta = \omega_0 t + \frac{1}{2}\alpha t^2$?
e: The linear analogue is $s = v_0 t + \frac{1}{2}at^2$.

q: Which linear kinematic equation is analogous to $\omega^2 = \omega_0^2 + 2\alpha \theta$?
e: The linear analogue is $v^2 = v_0^2 + 2as$.

q: Which linear kinematic equation is analogous to $\theta = \frac{\omega + \omega_0}{2}t$?
e: The linear analogue is $s = \frac{v + v_0}{2}t$.

q: What creates the cycle of day and night according to the text?
a: Artificial satellites going around the earth
Rotation of earth about its own axis
e: The rotation of earth about its own axis creates the cycle of day and night.

q: What happens to the angular velocity of an object when it speeds up or slows down during rotation?
e: When an object speeds up or slows down, its angular velocity is changing.

q: The kinematic equations for rotational motion are derived for an object under what condition?
e: The equations are derived for rotational motion under constant angular acceleration.

q: How do all particles of an object rotating around the axis of rotation move?
e: All particles of an object rotating around the axis of rotation move in a circular path.

q: In a rotating rigid body, the circular path of all particles lies on a plane that is in what orientation to the axis?
a: At a $45^\circ$ angle to the axis
e: The circular path lies on a plane that is perpendicular to the axis.

q: Where does the centre of rotation lie for the particles of a rotating rigid body?
a: On the edge of the rigid body
e: The centre of rotation lies on the axis.

q: What is the relation between arc length $s$ and angular displacement $\theta$?
e: The relation is $s = r\theta$.

q: In the equation $s = r\theta$, what unit must the angular displacement $\theta$ be measured in?
e: The angular displacement $\theta$ must be measured in radians.

q: What is the relation between the magnitude of linear velocity $v$ and angular velocity $\omega$?
e: The relation is $v = r\omega$.

q: Since the direction of linear velocity is tangent to the path, what is it also called?
e: Linear velocity is also called tangential velocity.

q: Is the instantaneous angular velocity $\omega$ of a rotational object the same for all particles?
a: Yes, it is the same for all particles.
No, it varies with the radius.
No, it is only the same on the axis.
e: The instantaneous angular velocity $\omega$ is the same for all particles comprising the object.

q: If the magnitude of the angular velocity changes, what kind of acceleration does the object have?
e: A change in the magnitude of angular velocity gives rise to tangential acceleration.

q: What is the direction of tangential acceleration?
a: Towards the centre of the circular path
Perpendicular to the plane of rotation
Always tangent to the circular path
e: The direction of tangential acceleration is always tangent to the circular path.

q: What is the relation between tangential acceleration $a_T$ and angular acceleration $\alpha$?
e: The relation is $a_T = r\alpha$.

q: The tangential acceleration of a rotating object is a measure of what?
a: How fast the angular displacement changes.
How fast the tangential velocity changes.
How fast the centripetal acceleration changes.
e: Tangential acceleration measures how fast the tangential velocity changes.

q: What is the direction of the angular velocity vector?
a: Towards the centre of the circular path
Perpendicular to the plane of rotation, and along the axis
e: The angular velocity vector is perpendicular to the plane of rotation and along the axis.

q: Which rule is usually used to specify the direction of angular velocity?
e: The direction is usually specified by the right-hand rule.

q: When applying the right-hand rule, what do the fingers represent?
a: The direction of the angular acceleration vector
The direction of the centripetal acceleration
e: The fingers point in the direction of rotation.

q: When applying the right-hand rule, what does the thumb point in the direction of?
e: The thumb points in the direction of the angular velocity vector.

q: When the angular velocity is increasing, in what direction does the angular acceleration vector point?
a: In the same direction as the angular velocity
e: When angular velocity is increasing, angular acceleration points in the same direction.

q: When the angular velocity is decreasing, in what direction does the angular acceleration vector point?
a: In the same direction as the angular velocity
e: When angular velocity is decreasing, angular acceleration points opposite to it.

q: In the relation $v = r\omega$, what does $r$ represent?
e: $r$ represents the radius of the circle.

q: Which quantity is the same for every particle of a rotational object?
e: The instantaneous angular velocity $\omega$ is the same for all particles.

q: In the relation $v = r\omega$, what does $\omega$ represent?
e: $\omega$ represents the angular velocity.

q: What is the direction of the linear velocity vector for a particle in circular motion?
e: The direction of linear velocity is tangent to the path.

q: If the angular acceleration $\alpha$ is zero, what is the value of the tangential acceleration $a_T$?
e: Since $a_T = r\alpha$, if $\alpha$ is zero, $a_T$ is zero.

q: The relation $a_T = r\alpha$ applies to which particles of a rotational object?
a: Every particle of the rotational object
e: The relation applies to every particle of the rotational object.

q: What physical quantity is represented by the symbol $\alpha$?
e: $\alpha$ represents angular acceleration.

q: An object that moves in a circle at constant speed $v$ is said to experience what kind of motion?
a: Rotational motion under constant angular acceleration
e: Moving in a circle at constant speed is uniform circular motion.

q: In uniform circular motion, what happens to the magnitude of the velocity?
a: It decreases at a constant rate.
e: The magnitude of the velocity remains constant in uniform circular motion.

q: In uniform circular motion, what happens to the direction of the velocity?
e: The direction of the velocity continuously changes as the object moves around the circle.

q: Why is an object revolving in a circle continuously accelerated even when its speed remains constant?
a: Because the magnitude of velocity is changing.
Because the direction of velocity continuously changes.
Because the mass of the object is changing.
e: The change in direction of velocity constitutes an acceleration.

q: As the time interval $\Delta t$ approaches zero, in what direction does the change in velocity vector $\Delta v$ point?
a: Towards the centre of the circle
Away from the centre of the circle
e: $\Delta v$ is essentially perpendicular to the velocities and points toward the centre.

q: Acceleration $a$ is in the same direction as $\Delta v$, therefore it points towards the centre. What is this acceleration called?
e: This acceleration is called centripetal acceleration.

q: What is another name for centripetal acceleration?
e: Centripetal acceleration is also called radial acceleration.

q: Why is centripetal acceleration also called radial acceleration?
a: Because it is directed along the radius towards the centre.
Because it is directed tangent to the path.
Because it is measured in radians.
e: It is directed along the radius towards the centre of the circle.

q: What is the formula for the magnitude of centripetal acceleration $a_c$ in terms of $v$ and $r$?
e: The formula is $a_c = \frac{v^2}{r}$.

q: By substituting $v = r\omega$ into the centripetal acceleration formula, what is the expression for $a_c$?
e: Substituting $v = r\omega$ gives $a_c = r\omega^2$.

q: In uniform circular motion, what is the angle between the centripetal acceleration vector and the linear velocity vector?
e: They are perpendicular to each other at every point in the path.

q: In uniform circular motion, where does the centripetal acceleration vector point?
a: Towards the centre of the circular path
e: It points towards the centre of the circular path.

q: In uniform circular motion, what is the direction of the linear velocity vector?
a: Towards the centre of the circular path
Perpendicular to the plane of rotation
e: The linear velocity vector is tangential to the path.

q: In nonuniform circular motion, how is the object moving?
a: In a straight line with varying speed.
In a circular path with a constant speed.
In a circular path with a varying speed.
e: In nonuniform circular motion, the object moves in a circular path with a varying speed.

q: In nonuniform circular motion, what gives rise to the tangential acceleration?
e: The angular acceleration gives rise to the tangential acceleration.

q: In nonuniform circular motion, the resultant acceleration is the vector sum of which two accelerations?
e: It is the vector sum of centripetal and tangential accelerations.

q: What is the formula for the magnitude of the resultant acceleration $a$ in nonuniform circular motion?
e: The magnitude is $a = \sqrt{a_c^2 + a_T^2}$.

q: What is the formula for the direction of the resultant acceleration $a$ (angle $\phi$)?
e: The direction is given by $\tan \phi = \frac{a_T}{a_c}$.

q: In nonuniform circular motion, what is the geometric relationship between $a_c$ and $a_T$ vectors?
a: They are parallel to each other.
They are perpendicular to each other.
e: The two acceleration vectors $a_c$ and $a_T$ are perpendicular to each other.

q: Unlike tangential acceleration, in which types of circular motion is centripetal acceleration present?
a: Both uniform and nonuniform circular motion
e: Centripetal acceleration is present in both uniform and nonuniform circular motion.

q: In the derivation of centripetal acceleration, the triangle formed by radius and arc is geometrically similar to what?
a: The vector triangle of the change in velocity
The triangle formed by tangential acceleration
The triangle formed by angular displacement
e: It is geometrically similar to the vector triangle of the change in velocity.

q: From the similar triangles in the derivation of centripetal acceleration, what is $\frac{\Delta v}{v}$ equal to?
e: The similar triangles give $\frac{\Delta v}{v} = \frac{\Delta s}{r}$.

q: In the derivation of centripetal acceleration, what does the limit of $\frac{\Delta s}{\Delta t}$ as $\Delta t \to 0$ represent?
e: The limit represents the linear speed $v$ of the object.

q: If an object is in nonuniform circular motion, what two components make up its resultant acceleration?
e: The resultant acceleration consists of radial (centripetal) and tangential components.

q: What causes the angular speed of an object to change in nonuniform circular motion?
e: The varying speed (magnitude of velocity) causes the angular speed to change.

q: Which acceleration is responsible for changing the direction of the velocity vector in circular motion?
e: Centripetal acceleration changes the direction of the velocity vector.

q: Which acceleration is responsible for changing the magnitude of the velocity vector in nonuniform circular motion?
e: Tangential acceleration changes the magnitude of the velocity (speed).

q: If the resultant acceleration vector makes an angle $\phi$ with $a_c$, what is $\tan \phi$ equal to?
e: $\tan \phi$ is equal to $\frac{a_T}{a_c}$.

q: In the vector diagram for change in velocity as $\Delta t \to 0$, what is the relationship between $\Delta v$ and $v_1$, $v_2$?
a: $\Delta v$ is essentially perpendicular to both.
$\Delta v$ is at a $45^\circ$ angle to both.
e: $\Delta v$ is essentially perpendicular to both $v_1$ and $v_2$.

q: Average acceleration has been defined as the change in velocity $\Delta v$ divided by what?
e: Average acceleration is $\frac{\Delta v}{\Delta t}$.

q: In the derivation of $a_c$, as $\Delta t$ approaches zero, the distance $\Delta s$ and angle $\Delta \theta$ become what?
e: As $\Delta t$ approaches zero, $\Delta s$ and $\Delta \theta$ become very small.

q: As $\Delta t$ approaches zero, the velocity vector $v_2$ will be almost parallel to what?
a: The change in velocity vector $\Delta v$
e: $v_2$ will be almost parallel to $v_1$.

q: In the equation $a_c = \lim_{\Delta t \to 0} \frac{\Delta v}{\Delta t}$, what does the limit represent?
e: The limit represents the instantaneous centripetal acceleration.

q: For uniform circular motion, the centripetal acceleration and linear velocity are what to each other?
e: They are perpendicular to each other at every point.

q: In nonuniform circular motion, the angular speed is changing, therefore the object experiences what?
e: A changing angular speed means the object experiences angular acceleration.

q: In nonuniform circular motion, the resultant acceleration points at an angle between which two vectors?
e: It points at an angle between $a_c$ and $a_T$.

q: The magnitude of the resultant acceleration in nonuniform circular motion is found using which relationship?
e: It is found using the Pythagorean theorem: $a = \sqrt{a_c^2 + a_T^2}$.

q: If an object is moving in a circular path with a varying speed, what type of motion is it?
a: Rotational motion under constant angular acceleration
e: Moving in a circular path with varying speed is nonuniform circular motion.

q: What is the symbol used to denote centripetal acceleration?
e: Centripetal acceleration is denoted by $a_c$.

q: What is the symbol used to denote tangential acceleration?
e: Tangential acceleration is denoted by $a_T$.

q: What is the unit of angular acceleration $\alpha$ as mentioned in the text?
e: Angular acceleration is measured in radian per second squared.

q: What is the unit of angular velocity $\omega$ as mentioned in the text?
e: Angular velocity is measured in radian per second.

q: What provides the tangential acceleration of the rim of a car wheel when it starts moving?
a: The angular acceleration provided by the engine
The linear velocity of the car
e: The angular acceleration provided by the engine results in tangential acceleration.

q: In nonuniform circular motion, unlike tangential acceleration, centripetal acceleration is what?
a: Present in both uniform and nonuniform circular motion
Only present when speed is constant
e: Centripetal acceleration is present in both uniform and nonuniform circular motion.

q: The change in direction of velocity constitutes what?
e: The change in direction of velocity constitutes an acceleration.

q: The magnitude of velocity remains constant in what motion?
e: The magnitude of velocity remains constant in uniform circular motion.

q: In uniform circular motion, $v_1 = v = v_2$ means what is constant?
e: It means the speed (magnitude of velocity) is constant.

q: The vector sum of centripetal and tangential accelerations gives what?
e: It gives the resultant acceleration of the object.

q: The direction of tangential acceleration is always what to the circular path?
e: The direction of tangential acceleration is always tangent to the circular path.

q: The direction of centripetal acceleration is along what?
e: It is directed along the radius towards the centre of the circle.
